note.label: Isaiah 38: Hezekiah's Sickness and the Fifteen Added Years

precepts.why:
The same account is recorded in Kings, word for word: “In those days was Hezekiah sick unto death. And the prophet Isaiah the son of Amoz came to him, and said unto him, Thus saith the Lord, Set thine house in order; for thou shalt die, and not live.”

Two witnesses to Hezekiah’s sickness and to Isaiah’s word that he set his house in order, for he would die and not live. It was after this that Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall, reminded the Most High how he had “walked before thee in truth and with a perfect heart”, and wept sore, and the Most High heard the prayer, saw the tears, and added fifteen years to his days.

precepts.text: The parallel record of the sundial sign brought backward ten degrees.
precepts.point: The sign given was the shadow on the sundial of Ahaz brought back ten degrees. The prophet had told them it was a light thing to make the sundial go forward ten degrees, so instead the sun returned backward ten degrees as the sign to Hezekiah.

note.label: Isaiah 38: Hezekiah's Sickness and the Fifteen Added Years

precepts.why:
Kings gives the fuller record of the sign of the sundial. “And Isaiah said, This sign shalt thou have of the Lord, that the Lord will do the thing that he hath spoken: shall the shadow go forward ten degrees, or go back ten degrees?” Hezekiah was given the choice, and answered, “It is a light thing for the shadow to go down ten degrees: nay, but let the shadow return backward ten degrees.”

It was a light thing to make the sundial go forward ten degrees, so instead the sun returned backward ten degrees as the sign to Hezekiah. “And Isaiah the prophet cried unto the Lord: and he brought the shadow ten degrees backward, by which it had gone down in the dial of Ahaz.” That is the sign of Isaiah 38:8, “the shadow of the degrees, which is gone down in the sun dial of Ahaz, ten degrees backward”, the Lord’s proof that he would do the thing he had spoken: add fifteen years to Hezekiah and deliver the city out of the hand of the king of Assyria.

points: In those days Hezekiah was sick unto death, and Isaiah the son of Amoz came and told him to set his house in order, for he would die and not live. Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed, reminding the Most High how he had walked before him in truth and with a perfect heart, and he wept sore.

note.label: Isaiah 38: Hezekiah's Sickness and the Fifteen Added Years

points: The word of the Lord came again to Isaiah: the Most High had heard the prayer and seen the tears, and would add fifteen years to Hezekiah's days and deliver the city out of the hand of the king of Assyria.

note.label: Isaiah 38: Hezekiah's Sickness and the Fifteen Added Years

points: The sign given was the shadow on the sundial of Ahaz brought back ten degrees. The prophet had told them it was a light thing to make the sundial go forward ten degrees, so instead the sun returned backward ten degrees as the sign to Hezekiah.

note.label: Isaiah 38: Hezekiah's Sickness and the Fifteen Added Years

points: This is the writing of Hezekiah after he had been sick and recovered. He speaks of being deprived of the residue of his years, going to the gates of the grave, his life cut off like a weaver cuts the thread.

note.label: Isaiah 38: Hezekiah's Sickness and the Fifteen Added Years

points: He testifies that the Most High cast all his sins behind his back and delivered his soul from the pit of corruption. The grave cannot praise him and death cannot celebrate him; the living, the living shall praise him, and the father makes his truth known to the children.

note.label: Isaiah 38: Hezekiah's Sickness and the Fifteen Added Years

points: Isaiah had said to take a lump of figs and lay it as a plaster upon the boil that he might recover, and Hezekiah had asked what the sign was that he should go up to the house of the Lord.
